method: Read the new upload-registration association, exact part/completion checks, full completed-file gate and final action-release gate. Matched them to the already reviewed preparation/credential/request/receipt code and checked the final source hash. No credential or private execution-receipt contents were opened; no client, network, test, upload or compile was run by this reviewer.
findings: A source-byte PUT requires the existing paper/draft/current remote metadata verification and a successful registration response bound to the same paper, draft API path, exact manifest filename, metadata hash, full file-manifest hash and exact registration-body hash. The actual returned uploadId must match, and the reported part capacity must cover the entire verified source file. Only the fixed part-one endpoint is used; no returned arbitrary URL or redirect receives credentials or bytes.

The part body is the exact in-memory source byte sequence already checked against the authenticated release manifest and local file SHA/size. Upload completion additionally requires a successful PUT receipt for this same draft/upload/file, metadata and full manifest with the exact source-body SHA. No PDF, archive, credential, bulk asset or arbitrary local path is newly uploadable.

Source-check and preview-status GETs require successful completion receipts for all three expected files, each tied back to a reviewed registration. Their request paths remain fixed-origin submission paths with validated identifiers. Those reads can obtain the live source-tree hashes/schema for the next stage, but this audit does not infer that the remote set or revision already matches the local manifest.

The final explicit release gate blocks both preview POST and commit before credential loading. Thus no remote compiler or publication operation is enabled by this version. A later release must verify the actual complete staged set, byte hashes/sourceTreeDigest and exact revision before private compilation, then bind successful preview evidence and unknown-result protections before commit.

Intent/response request IDs, manifest_file, metadata/full-manifest/payload hashes and sanitized owner-only receipts remain. There is one manual request per invocation, no automatic retries and no inferred idempotency for registration/completion. Unknown mutation outcomes require bound status inspection before repeating. Existing origin, redirect/proxy, credential, release-file and watchdog protections are unchanged. Remote compilation timing remains the coordinator's separate responsibility.
resolved_findings: Kept preview POST disabled until live staged-source evidence is available and bound.
